argument: Building on her view that emotions are valuable appraisals of reality rather than irrational spasms, Martha Nussbaum argues that our democracies are failing not because the system itself is broken, but because a toxic climate of unexamined fear has overtaken political discourse and made the trust, cooperation, and civil dialogue democracy depends on impossible. Fear is a primal emotion rooted in infant helplessness that politicians and media deliberately stoke, and when it becomes the driving force behind anger, disgust, and envy, those emotions turn toxic to democratic life. Her solutions run through ending segregation, for instance with a mandatory youth civil service program, and through cultivating practical hope: an orientation that must be willed daily and requires real engagement with the issues and a reasonably concrete picture of the future we want.
keyIdeas: Emotions, properly examined, are appraisals of what we value, so ignoring them means missing huge pieces of how societies and relationships function at a basic level.

Comparing guilt and shame shows that which emotion is more constructive depends on the society: guilt, which acknowledges the rights of the wronged person, fits a democracy built on trust and cooperation, while shame could serve a different power structure.

Fear develops in infancy from the asymmetry between being physically helpless and cognitively aware, and this primal circuitry lurks in us for life, ready to be stirred up by con artists, politicians, and media companies who know that fear sells.

Fear begins unexamined and reactionary, and when it becomes the primary force behind anger, disgust, and envy it turns them toxic, pushing anger toward retribution, envy toward class warfare, and disgust onto entire groups of people.

The flip side of fear is hope, which also responds to uncertainty but surges forward and creates possibilities, and practical hope, unlike idle hope, must be willed every day and demands enough engagement to have a concrete picture of the future you want.

terms.def: Nussbaum's name for a political climate where constant fear of threats and of each other drives people to gather under a strong absolute leader, since fear is the currency that makes monarchy work and makes democracy fail.
A narcissistic, inward-looking emotion arising from failing an ideal standard of perfection you set for yourself, fixed by making yourself feel better rather than repairing any wrong.
A negative emotion that fundamentally acknowledges the rights of the person who was wronged, and whose fix is doing something to repair the wrong done to them.
Nussbaum's description of babies, who need to be tyrannical because of the asymmetry between their physical helplessness and their cognitive awareness, the stage where fear first develops.
Hope as a syndrome rather than a mere emotion: an orientation willed daily that requires a reasonably concrete picture of the desired future, gained only through engagement with the issues.

anchors: FIXING feelings of SHAME, is always about making YOURSELF feel better…while fixing GUILT…is a person DOING something that REPAIRS the wrong that was DONE to another person.
you can ALSO imagine how SHAME…in some OTHER kind of society, with a DIFFERENT kind of power structure, DIFFERENT social norms…shame you can imagine in THAT world…would be a FAR more useful emotion
maybe what has changed in recent years is NOT that the system has proven to be a failure…but that maybe a TOXIC level of FEAR, as an emotion…has OVERTAKEN our political discourse
babies NEED to be little tyrants…in part because of this asymmetry between how physically HELPLESS they are, and how cognitively AWARE they are of what’s going on AROUND them.
you’re SMUGGLING IN the entire democratic process… that is EXAMINING that fear response… and then TURNING it into something productive.
the ANSWER is going to be when the more PRIMARY emotion of FEAR, becomes the driving FORCE BEHIND these emotions.
if the people on the ground in a democracy don’t understand the rule or don’t think it should BE a rule…people are just not going to FOLLOW it.
Getting people to have these toxic levels of FEAR about an ENTIRE group of people…almost always REQUIRES you to know almost nothing about them.
FEAR sees uncertainty and shrinks back, HOPE on the other hand EXPANDS and surges FORWARD. Fear causes us to REMOVE possibilities, Hope seeks to bring about NEW ones.
it ALSO becomes something… that requires a reasonably concrete picture of what we want the future to look like.
